frontier.hypothesis: The guard block is reachable only by changing WHERE loop.c inserts the third loop's invariant hoists relative to the pre-loop `*(arg0+0x18) += 0xC` store - the store must be RTL-later than the two invariant loads, since sched.c can never move a symbol_ref load above an aliasing base-register store.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c sched_analyze records a data dependence from insn 253 (the sw through (plus (reg s1) 24)) to insns 479/482/480 (the symbol_ref loads) because GCC 2.7.2's memory disambiguation cannot separate a symbol MEM from a base-register MEM. loop.c hoists invariants into the preheader, which sits after every pre-loop statement, so the loads can only precede the store if they are emitted from an EARLIER loop's preheader or from a different structural position.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80070C70/dumps/text1b.loop for where the D_800A3558/D_800A35B0 invariants are moved and which basic block becomes the third loop's preheader; then test STRUCTURAL (not spelling) variants that change preheader placement - e.g. putting the second (6-iteration) loop and the third loop in the same enclosing block, or making the increment store part of the second loop's tail. Do NOT re-sweep guard-region spelling, mode-test/bound operand order, initialiser position, declaration order, or explicit invariant carriers: 317 spellings this session cover all five and none goes below 7.

frontier.hypothesis: The 2-insn entry tie (insn 49 `s0 = 0` vs insn 71 `a0 = sp + 24`) is decided by INSN_PRIORITY, not by the dependence class, and the priority gap is set by how many in-block insns depend on the &prim address.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c:2408 rank_for_schedule compares INSN_PRIORITY first; priority() (sched.c:1504, where the BB2_PRIO_DEBUG hook prints it) is the longest dependence path to the end of the block. Insn 71 feeds the first call's argument; insn 49 has no in-block dependents, yet OUR scheduler emits 49 first, which a pure priority comparison should not produce - so either the priorities are equal (making it a class/LUID decision) or the model is wrong.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the TU under the INSTRUMENTED cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, i.e. `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80070C70 -Instrumented`) with BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1 and BB2_RANK_DEBUG=1 in the environment, capture stderr to tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s17/, and grep for UIDs 49 and 71 to read their INSN_PRIORITY values and the class-tie decision directly. The source-side levers are exhausted: 13 initialiser positions, three first-loop chassis forms and 147 declaration-order spellings are all inert at 7.
